title: Feature workspaces: branch out, sync, and update from Git
objective_text: Work the way branched workspaces do in Git: a feature branch from main's latest commit, a commit on it, an update from main after another PR lands, and your PR completed into main.
scenario: The Ingest workspace is connected to main. Ana and Ben each branched out to a workspace of their own. Ana's dedupe change is approved; Ben (you) still has to make the copy retry 3 times. A hotfix landed on main this morning, and the team's branch policy only completes a PR whose branch has main's latest commit.
engine_label: Git on this PC, in a repository made for this exercise

commits.message: Add the Ingest pipeline and the Orders notebook
Drop duplicate orders in the notebook
Hotfix: give the copy two hours

verifies: Your Git session, run with Git on this PC, leaves your change on feature/ben-retry, that branch updated with main after Ana's PR, and main holding both features and the hotfix, with no merge left unfinished.
does_not_verify: Fabric's Branches tab: Branch out to another workspace, the workspace it creates, or which items it copies.
Fabric's Update all, the Changes and Updates counts, or that commits are disabled while updates are waiting.
Pull requests and branch policies in Azure DevOps or GitHub: here you complete them as merges yourself.

expected.description: feature/ben-retry: your retry commit and a merge of main after Ana's PR; main: both PRs merged, retry 3 and timeout 0.02:00:00, the notebook dropping duplicate orders.

validation.fail: Your work isn't on a feature branch of its own.

rules.why: A merge isn't done until its result is committed.
Branch out gives each developer a branch (and workspace) of their own; main changes only through PRs.

validation.fail: Your branch wasn't updated from main before its PR completed.
validation.pass: feature/ben-retry has main's latest commits, Ana's included.

rules.why: The branch policy needs main's latest commit in your branch, and main has Ana's PR in it by then.

validation.fail: main doesn't have both features and the hotfix.
validation.pass: main has Ana's dedupe, your retries and the two-hour timeout.

rules.why: Ana's PR completes into main before yours, so main has her work even without your merge.

json.why: Write your change on top of the file as main has it; an old copy undoes the hotfix.

hints: git switch -c feature/ben-retry main starts your branch from main as it is now.
Write the pipeline file as main has it, with only retry changed.
Complete Ana's PR first: switch to main and merge feature/ana-dedupe with --no-ff, as a PR completion does.
Then switch back to your branch and merge main into it before you merge it into main with --no-ff.
explanation: Branch out to another workspace creates a new Git branch from the last commit of the source workspace's branch and connects a workspace to it, so each developer works apart from main. You commit there, and a pull request takes the work back to main. When other work reaches main first, your branch is behind: updating it from main brings that work in, so your PR is tested and completed against what main really has. In Fabric, a workspace whose branch has new commits shows them under Updates, and commits are disabled until you update.
reset: Reset rebuilds the repository from the exercise's history and puts the starter session back.
review_notes: The pipeline and notebook files are cut down to the fields the exercise uses.

Checked on Microsoft Learn 2026-11-07: Branch out creates a new branched workspace (or switches an existing one) to a new Git branch made from the last commit of the source workspace (git-integration-process, branched-workspace); the feature workflow is commit to the feature branch, then a PR to main (branched-workspace); each workspace connects to one branch (manage-branches); "If there were updates made to the Git branch, commits are disabled until you update your workspace", and Update always updates the whole branch to its latest commit (git-integration-process). The branch policy is the team's own, set in the Git provider.
